reason: Sunlight can drive evaporation from the sea, beginning a route back to shore as fresh water.
expectation: Solar heating should evaporate some seawater.

effect: Evaporation leaves most dissolved minerals behind, providing water vapor for the freshwater cycle.
reaction: The separation of water from dissolved minerals is a satisfying link to fresh rain.
reason: Cooler air should help the evaporated water condense into clouds.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

expectation: Water vapor will condense into droplets or clouds.

effect: The evaporated seawater has condensed into a cloud, advancing the freshwater cycle.
reaction: The connection between evaporation and fresh cloud water is clear.
reason: Wind can carry the cloud toward land, where it may return water to the shore.
expectation: The wind will move the cloud toward the coast.

effect: Wind has carried the cloud over land, positioning it to return water to the shore.
reaction: The sea-to-land transport is a clear link in the water cycle.
reason: The rocky rise may cause the cloud to rise and produce rain.

choice.with: A rocky rise behind the shore

expectation: Air rising over the rocky rise will cool and produce rainfall.

effect: The cloud has produced rain on the rise, ready to flow back toward the shore.
reaction: The rising-air explanation makes the rainfall route clear.
reason: The slope should carry the rain downhill toward the basin and shore.

choice.with: A slope toward a broad basin

expectation: Fresh rainwater will run down the slope toward the shore.

effect: The stream completes the fresh-water return goal; moonlight remains to be brought to the shore.
reaction: The water cycle returning to the sea is a satisfying conclusion to that route.
reason: The Moon and sea are the clearest available pieces for leaving moonlight on the water.

choice.combine: The Moon with a pale early crust

expectation: Moonlight will appear on the sea, perhaps requiring calmer water afterward.

effect: The sea was not a compatible partner, but the feedback automatically paired the Moon with a tidal pool and completed the remaining goal.
reaction: I was surprised the direct sea pairing failed, though the reflected Moon made a fitting ending.

mostWorthwhile.text: Tracing seawater through evaporation, rain and runoff was worthwhile: it showed how water returns fresh while most dissolved minerals remain behind.

leastWorthwhile.text: Condensing the vapor into a cloud was clear but predictable after evaporation; it felt less revealing than the rest of the route.

surprise.text: The Moon could not be combined directly with the sea, but compatibility feedback automatically produced its reflection in a rock pool.

arbitrary.text: The failed Moon-and-sea pairing felt somewhat arbitrary because the goal explicitly allowed moonlight on the sea; the pool route was clear once revealed.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for more connected explanations of natural processes, especially if the next chapter offered similarly concrete discoveries.
